newsitem.title: USA: Sparks pegs 1996-97 US soy stocks 115 mln bu-trade.
newsitem.headline: Sparks pegs 1996-97 US soy stocks 115 mln bu-trade.

text.p: Sparks Companies pegged 1996-97 (Sept/Aug) U.S. soybean ending stocks at 115 million bushels and new crop 1997-98 stocks at 123 million bushels, trade sources said.
The U.S. Agriculture Department in its June report put 1996-97 stocks at 130 million bushels and new crop ending supplies at 240 million bushels.
A spokesman for the Memphis-based analytical firm was not available for comment on the projections.
Trade sources said Sparks' new crop stocks figure differed from USDA's largely because of lower crop projections.

Sparks reportedly put 1997 U.S. soybean acreage at 67.5 million acres, below USDA's June 1 outlook for 68.8 million. Trade sources said Sparks put yield at 38.4 bushels per acre, against USDA's 38.5 bushels.
Sparks also factored in higher demand rates than USDA, one trade source said. Sparks' export figure was 986 million bushels, compared with USDA's 910 million.
Sparks did not factor in any imports during the 1997-98 crop year, while USDA estimated five million bushels in imports, trade sources said.
